title: Tom Farmer, CIA general counsel, vetting Paperclip Germans

tellings.quote: I was going to say it turned out he was involved in in the project called Paperclip.

plain: Tom Farmer, who served as general counsel (chief lawyer) of the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, was involved in Project Paperclip, the American effort to bring German scientists to the United States after the Second World War, and helped vet the Germans. The presidential advisor Harold Malmgren tells this about a man he knew personally, saying "it turned out he was involved" in the project. It matters to his account because it puts a man he knew close to the people who handled secret technology after the war.
